classification.difficultyReason: Use equal opposite sides to form simultaneous equations, solve for two pronumerals, and calculate the perimeter.

content.prompt:
In the rectangle $ABCD$,
$$AB=p+2q,\quad BC=3p-10,\quad CD=5(p-q)\quad\text{and}\quad DA=2q+3.$$
Find the perimeter of the rectangle.

answer.short:
$52$ units.

Equate opposite sides and solve the resulting simultaneous equations.
answer.worked:
Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal, so
$$\begin{align*}p+2q&=5(p-q)\\p+2q&=5p-5q\\4p-7q&=0\qquad(1)\\3p-10&=2q+3\\3p-2q&=13\qquad(2)\end{align*}$$
Multiply (1) by $2$ and (2) by $7$:
$$\begin{align*}8p-14q&=0\qquad(3)\\21p-14q&=91\qquad(4)\end{align*}$$
Subtract (3) from (4):
$$\begin{align*}13p&=91\\p&=7\end{align*}$$
Substitute into (2):
$$\begin{align*}21-2q&=13\\-2q&=-8\\q&=4\end{align*}$$
The side lengths and perimeter are
$$\begin{align*}AB&=7+2(4)\\AB&=15\\BC&=3(7)-10\\BC&=11\\P&=2(15+11)\\P&=52.\end{align*}$$
Check: $CD=5(7-4)=15=AB$ and $DA=2(4)+3=11=BC$. Hence the perimeter is $52$ units.
